passage: In the study hall of the boarding school, Rashmi's phone lay face up beside her chemistry notes. Jatin's message had been sitting there since 7:40: "u ok? u left dinner early." She had read it eleven times. She wasn't going to answer. If she said what was wrong, that he'd laughed along when the others mocked her accent at dinner, he would probably say, "Relax, you're overreacting." Silence felt safer. Silence felt like the one thing she could control. Ramesh sir walked between the desks, checking that phones were away. Rashmi slid hers under her notebook but kept one corner visible, just in case it lit up again. Part of her wanted Jatin to keep trying. To notice. To come and find her.

qa.q: Since what time had Jatin's message been sitting there?
qa.a: It had been sitting there since 7:40.

qa.q: Why does Rashmi choose not to reply?
qa.a: She fears hearing "you're overreacting", so silence feels safer and gives her some control.

qa.q: What turning point is available to Rashmi now?
qa.a: She could reply briefly with the real reason, "The accent jokes at dinner hurt", rather than waiting for Jatin to guess.

qa.q: What is Jatin likely experiencing as his message goes unanswered?
qa.a: Jatin is probably unsure and uneasy, noticing something is wrong but not knowing what he did.

grounding: Shows a teen girl withholding a reply because silence feels safer than a fight, while hoping her friend will notice and come to her.

passage:
Dear Uday,
I'm not going to send this. That's kind of the point. You've texted me four times since Saturday's practice, and I've left every one on "seen". I know it's mean. But if I reply, I'll have to say that it hurt when you told Coach I wasn't ready for the relay, like I'm the weakest girl on the team, and you'll say I'm too sensitive, and then we'll fight, and I'll cry, and you'll win. Not replying means I don't lose. It's the only part of this I'm in charge of. And honestly? Some small, silly part of me hopes you'll keep texting. That you'll show up at my gate and say, "Pallavi, what's wrong?" Then I'd know you actually care.
Your friend (for now)

qa.q: How many times has Uday texted since Saturday's practice?
qa.a: Uday has texted four times since Saturday's practice.

qa.q: What does Pallavi secretly hope will happen?
qa.a: She hopes Uday will keep texting and even come to her gate asking what's wrong, which would prove Uday cares.

qa.q: What could Pallavi try instead of leaving every message on "seen"?
qa.a: She could send one honest line, "What you told Coach hurt me", and ask Uday to hear it without calling her sensitive.

qa.q: What might Uday be feeling after four unanswered texts?
qa.a: Uday may feel worried and shut out, unable to guess what went wrong, and might soon stop trying.

grounding: Shows a teen girl choosing silence as protection from a fight and from being called too sensitive, while hoping her friend will come to her.
